[i]The convoy rolled to a halt at the front entrance of the New Rorack Diplomatic Center, its glass façade gleaming under the muted afternoon light. As the doors opened, Oceanice D.E.S.F. guards stepped out first, forming a protective corridor with practiced precision.

Then came President Ironvisak Willham, dressed strikingly in the formal uniform of the old Oceanice Republic, that immediately drew subtle glances from nearby staff. Everyone inside the Diplomatic Center already knew of todays meeting; the press had gathered for days to get information about the meeting. But even with all the preparation, the sheer presence of the D.E.S.F. escort, combined with Willhams historical attire, brought a quiet tension to the hall.

A Lavian security officer approached with a welcoming gesture. 
 Welcome, Mr. President. This way, please.

He led the group forward through the expansive lobby, where models of Lavian engineering projects stood proudly on polished platforms: experimental rail systems, naval vessels, and aerospace prototypes arranged between seating areas and a pristine café buzzing with diplomatic staff.
Dr. Kals Decvier and Dr. Helena Veyra walked close behind the president, eyeing both the displays and the alert posture of the Lavian security personnel, who were clearly adjusting to the scale of the Oceanice security detail.

As they passed beneath a suspended model of an MB-157 interceptor, it caught the President's eye. Willham paused for a moment.

Look at that, he murmured. Its rare to see an old era plane preserved so well. Dr. Helena followed his gaze. A reminder, Mr. President that era is behind us. Now its time to change our history and move toward a better cause. Willham nodded, straightening his uniform as if accepting both the weight of the past and the responsibility ahead.
 Exactly. Today, we negotiate not as heirs of our nations pasts... but for a better future which we hope to lead.

The group continued onward, stepping through a secure frame into the main conference chamber. The room opened before them with polished wood paneling, warm diffused lighting, and two long rows of flags of Oceanice and Lavian standing opposite one another.[/i]

[b]December 18, 2026: IDF no more[/b]

Following the Order for Reorganization that had been released in a private memo to the National Defense Forces, the First Council sought to rename and integrate further the private intelligence and private defense branches. 

Thus on December 18 in a meeting with the head of the National Security Staff (NSS) and the head of the Imperial Defense Forces (IDF) it was agreed that the functions of the two offices would be unified into a single commission known as the State Committee for Security and Information (SCSIS) thereby permitting the former IDF a broader scope of policing.

It was further agreed upon that the SCIS would be the primary internal policing body for the state, overseeing the individual police departments under a central organ. As a result of this a three stage plan was initiated for the implementation of the SCIS and its functions, with a completion date of January-February 2027 with extra time to remove redundancies in local police departments.

The move was a clear indication to the councils of the principalities that the state intended to instill order into every facet of government, with some worrying about a return to the days of the dictatorship. However, it was assured to the councils that the SCIS would operate under the framework of international law until new laws could be implemented.
